title: One Moment
description: Mordaine escalation beat 4 of 4 — the payoff, and the last beat before world1_throne_room_approach. She is discovered MID-PROCEDURE and finishes it before acknowledging anyone. Her novella fight is 'elegant, formal, systematic... as though she were running a test' (:781); being interrupted and calmly completing the gesture states her method before the fight demonstrates it. GRACEFUL DEGRADATION: the gesture is carried entirely by narration because CutsceneActor has no pose/animation step today (cowir-cutscenes msg 3099) and cannot reach her 256px battle-sheet 'summon' frames (cowir-sprites msg 3101). If a 32px cast pose + an await-completion pose step ever land, the two narration beats marked below are where it slots — the writing does not need it, but it would be better with it. Fires on first entry to Castle Harmonia floor 3. NOTE: `background` is INERT for presentation:staged (CutsceneDirector:258 — 'live world stays visible, no backdrop'); the real castle map is what the player sees. The key is set to an existing asset only so backdrop-existence ratchets stay green — it is NOT a claim this scene shows a throne room.

steps.text: She was mid-gesture when the door opened. One hand raised, holding a shape in the air that had not finished being a shape.

She did not stop. She finished it — the hand turned over, the shape settled into whatever it had been becoming, and the gesture ended the way a sentence ends: when the sentence is done, and not when somebody walks into the room.

lines.speaker: Mordaine
lines.text: ...There. That will hold until I am back.

steps.text: Nobody had asked what it was. Nobody asked now. There is a particular silence that arrives when a person does something incomprehensible in front of you with complete competence, and the party stood in it.

lines.speaker: Mordaine
lines.text: You may go up. I will be there before you are, and I will not have hurried.

lines.speaker: Mordaine
lines.text: Please don't read anything into that. It is only the shape of the building.

steps.text: It was, in fact, only the shape of the building. She had approved the plans.
